lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Revenue from four customers out of approximately 70 total customers represented approximately 63% of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
Revenue from five customers out of approximately 70 total customers represented approximately 67% of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, Iveda Taiwan’s operations accounted for 85% and 87% of our total revenue, respectively.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, Iveda Taiwan’s operations accounted for 93% and 71% of our total revenue, respectively.
78 % of the total accounts receivable at December 31, 2025 was from four customers out of a total of 42 customer accounts receivable accounts.
No other customers represented greater than 10% of total revenues in years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.

We regard certain aspects of our internal operations, products, and documentation as proprietary and rely on a combination of copyright and trademark (federal and common) laws, trade secrets, software security measures, license agreements, and nondisclosure agreements to protect our proprietary information.

Our ability to achieve and maintain annual profitability depends on a number of factors, including our ability to attract and service customers on a profitable basis and the growth of the video surveillance industry.
We Depend On Certain Key Personnel.
We Rely on Iveda Taiwan, Our Taiwan Subsidiary, For A Significant Portion of Our Revenue.
We Depend on Third Party Manufacturers and Suppliers for the Products We Sell.
Although we depend on third-party manufacturers and suppliers for the Products we sell, risks are minimized because we do not depend exclusively on any one manufacturer or supplier.
We rely on domestic and foreign suppliers to provide us with products in a timely manner and at favorable prices.
We Rely On Service Providers To Distribute Our Products To Customers.
We Depend On Our Intellectual Property.

We rely on a combination of copyright and trademark (federal and common) laws, trade secrets, software security measures, license agreements, and nondisclosure agreements to protect our proprietary information.
